title: How to put someone into the recovery position
intro: The recovery position keeps the airway open for a person who is unconscious but breathing normally. It lets fluid drain from the mouth and stops the tongue from blocking the throat. Knowing this simple technique can save a life while you wait for emergency help. Always call emergency services first.

sections.heading: When to use it
paragraphs: Use the recovery position when a person does not respond to you but is breathing normally, and there is no sign of serious injury to the neck or back that would make moving them dangerous. Common causes include fainting that does not quickly pass, epileptic seizures after the jerking stops, intoxication or illness.
If the person is not breathing normally, do not use the recovery position. Call emergency services and start chest compressions.

sections.heading: Check first
paragraphs: Shout and gently shake the shoulders. If there is no response, call for help, ask someone to call emergency services, and check the breathing by tilting the head back and lifting the chin for up to ten seconds. Look, listen and feel for normal breathing.

sections.heading: Steps to follow
paragraphs: Kneel beside the person. Place the arm nearest you at a right angle to the body with the palm facing up. Bring the far arm across the chest and hold the back of that hand against their cheek nearest you.

With your other hand, bend the far knee up, grasp it, and roll the person toward you onto their side. Adjust the upper leg so that both hip and knee are bent at right angles to keep them stable. Tilt the head back gently to keep the airway open, with the mouth facing downward so fluid can drain.

sections.heading: After positioning
paragraphs: Stay with the person and check breathing regularly until help arrives. Cover them to keep them warm. If breathing stops or changes, roll them onto their back and start resuscitation. If they must stay on their side for more than half an hour, turn them to the other side.
Tell the paramedics what happened, how long the person was unconscious, and any medicines or health conditions you know of.

sections.heading: Special situations
paragraphs: For a suspected spinal injury, avoid moving the person unless the airway is at risk. Pregnant women are best placed on their left side. Small children and babies need slight adjustments, and first-aid courses teach these. Learning first aid in a practical course gives much more confidence than reading alone.

examples.title: Helping after a fall
examples.text: Imagine a person collapses at a gathering, does not respond, but is breathing. You could ask someone to call emergency services, roll the person onto their side, tilt the head back and stay beside them until help arrives.

examples.title: Practising ahead
examples.text: Suppose you want to be ready for an emergency. You might join a local first-aid course where you can practise the recovery position on a mannequin and with a partner, and repeat the training every few years.
